newsitem.title: ITALY: European Albania mission gathers in Rome.
newsitem.headline: European Albania mission gathers in Rome.

text.p: A team of high-level European diplomats assembled in Rome on Monday on its way to Albania where it will assess how to help the country's new unity government restore order, diplomatic sources said.

They said members of the mission, led by Dutch diplomat Jan de Marchant et d'Ansembourg, were meeting at the Italian Foreign Ministry to coordinate their visit and were expected to arrive in Tirana by Italian military helicopter in the late afternoon.
The assessment mission, which is around 10-strong, is expected to stay in Tirana until Wednesday for meetings with Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and his ministers, the sources said.

Some of its members were also expected to visit the main port of Durres, a key bridgehead for any relief aid effort for the impoverished state, where weeks of armed unrest have left the country in chaos.
The team, whose visit was announced by European Union foreign ministers on Sunday, is due to pave the way for a larger advisory mission on civilian reconstruction and police and military matters.
It includes representatives from the Netherlands, which holds the EU presidency, Greece, Italy, the European Commission and the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
